chapter: Harlem youth, Monk and Bird, and Greensboro
title: Freddie Webster's sound and Miles's debt to him
summary: McLean describes Freddie Webster's sound as a big red ball and hears Miles absorbing it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Stop with Freddie Webster. His name comes up as having – describe his sound and what impact you think he had.

I saw him play twice. I saw him play that Sunday. His sound was like a big red ball, if you could imagine a guy with a trumpet like you’d blow a bubble from a bubble gum. You see a huge, shiny, red, beautiful ball come out of the front of his horn. Beautiful sound. Different than Fats or anybody. I heard him play like that. And then I heard him in Dizzy’s band the first time I heard Bird with Dizzy up at the McKinley Theater. He was in that band. I heard him play that day. Yeah, he was incredible. And I
can hear Miles’s influence from Freddie Webster. I can hear it. It’s very obvious that Miles was totally absorbed by Freddie’s playing, as well as Dizzy.
Tell now – I took you off, but tell us how the rest of that day unfolded.
